short: Mexico has no federal AI law. General-law initiatives are in committee in the Chamber of Deputies, with the deadline for an opinion extended to 31 August 2027; the new federal data protection law of March 2025 gives a right to object to automated decisions.
title: Mexico AI Laws
subtitle: No federal AI law: initiatives in committee, and the 2025 data protection law
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI act. Mexico has no federal AI law. In the Chamber of Deputies, initiatives to issue a General Law on Artificial Intelligence (expediente 7550) and a General Law for the Regulation and Ethical Use of AI (expediente 8135) are before the Science, Technology and Innovation committee, whose deadline to report on them was extended to 31 August 2027. The new Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (LFPDPPP), published in the Diario Oficial on 20 March 2025, gives people a right to object to automated processing that evaluates them without human intervention. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Chamber of Deputies' Gaceta Parlamentaria and its consolidated laws.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateStatus
Initiative issuing the General Law on Artificial IntelligenceExpediente 7550Turned to committee 29 April 2026In committee; opinion due by 31 August 2027
Initiative issuing the General Law for the Regulation and Ethical Use of AIExpediente 8135Turned to committee 17 June 2026In committee; opinion due by 31 August 2027
Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private PartiesNew law, DOF 20 March 2025; last amended DOF 14 November 202520 March 2025In force

Who regulates and enforces

  • Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno: imposes the LFPDPPP's sanctions (art. 59).

Scope and reach

No AI statute. The LFPDPPP gives a right to object to automated processing that evaluates a person without human intervention and produces unwanted legal effects (art. 26, fr. II).

Core obligations

  • Respect the right to object to automated decisions (LFPDPPP art. 26) and the law's other duties on personal data.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Infringements listed in art. 58, fr. VIII to XVIIIA fine of 200 to 320,000 times the Unit of Measure and Update (UMA)LFPDPPP art. 59, fr. IIISecretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno
Repeated infringementsAn additional 100 to 320,000 UMALFPDPPP art. 59, fr. IVSame
Infringements involving sensitive dataUp to twice the amounts aboveLFPDPPP art. 59Same

What is coming next

  • 31 August 2027: the extended deadline for the committee's opinion on initiatives 7550 and 8135.

Related

Sources

  • Gaceta Parlamentaria, 9 July 2026, Cámara de Diputados
  • LFPDPPP, consolidated text, Cámara de Diputados

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: AI initiatives in the Senate, and proposed constitutional amendments on AI.
